exposure: trial of labor after cesarean delivery
cohort: 1856 women contemplating a vaginal birth after a previous single low-transverse cesarean delivery, recruited between 34 and 38 weeks of gestation
finding: Incorporating lower uterine segment thickness measurement into the decision-making process for delivery route after a previous cesarean delivery resulted in a lower than expected rate of uterine rupture during trial of labor.
mod_finding: This study found that incorporating lower uterine segment thickness measurements into the decision-making process for trial of labor after cesarean delivery resulted in a low risk of uterine rupture.
